stories.headline: Jagan regrets YSRCP’s backing of 2023 Election Commissioner appointment law
stories.title: Jagan regrets YSRCP’s backing of 2023 Election Commissioner appointment law
reasons: source: event has 2 copies, primary source counted once
corroboration: 2 independent source groups -> high confidence
article_sentences: Amid protests against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSR Congress Party chief YS Jagan Mohan Reddy on Sunday, October 18, said he regretted supporting a law introduced by the BJP-led Union government that changed the process for appointing Election Commissioners.

Jagan made the remarks while accusing the State Election Commission of bias during nominations for local body elections in Andhra Pradesh, where political violence between the YSRCP and the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) has intensified.
Jagan said that the appointments of Election Commissioners should be “neutral.”
"Both the State Election Commissioners and the Chief Election Commissioners should not be nominated by the ruling parties.
In the past we have supported the Union government’s mechanism to make appointments by the ruling party.
But we regret it today.
We regret committing that mistake.
Because an examiner cannot be appointed by a student," he said.

YSRCP had backed the 2023 Bill in Parliament, where the President appoints the Election Commissioners based on the recommendation of a committee chaired by the Prime Minister and comprising the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
Seeking reforms in the nomination process, Jagan said, "Earlier, the selection committee included the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India.
The current arrangement gives two votes to the ruling side and one to the Opposition.
The Chief Justice is no longer part of the committee.

stories.headline: CJI announces virtual access to Supreme Court for Leh, Kargil lawyers
stories.title: CJI announces virtual access to Supreme Court for Leh, Kargil lawyers
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 18: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday said lawyers from Leh and Kargil would soon be able to virtually access the Supreme Court from the Ladakh Bench of the High Court. All matters originating from Ladakh would be listed on a single day and heard through video-conferencing, sparing lawyers and litigants the time, cost and hardship of travelling to Delhi, Justice Kant said as he inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh here. Describing the inauguration as a historic step, the CJI referred to the establishment of a Special Court in Leh in 1870, observing that while the institution had passed into history, the geographical challenges that restricted access to justice persisted for generations. "For close to a century, the high court that served Ladakh sat beyond the Great Himalayas, reachable in winter only by air," he said. The CJI said the insertion of the name 'Ladakh' in a high court after it became a Union Territory in 2019 was an important step, but the gesture remained largely symbolic. "A name on a court's letterhead is not the same as a court at one's doorstep," he said. Justice Kant emphasised that the bench belongs equally to Leh and Kargil – the two districts in the Union Territory — and said its purpose would be served only when people in every corner of Ladakh start to feel a sense of ownership over the institution. He also said that once video-conferencing facilities have been set up at the bench, the Supreme Court would list all matters originating from Ladakh on a single day and hear them on a day-to-day basis virtually. The arrangement, the CJI said, would enable members of the Leh and Kargil bar associations to argue cases before the top court without leaving Ladakh. "In this way, the distance will no longer stand between people of Ladakh and the highest Court of our country," he said. Justice Kant said that the true measure of a court is not its geographical elevation but its accessibility to the people it serves. "We are some 3,500 metres above the sea, and I am told no high court in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves," he said. The CJI recalled the role of village institutions and customary practices in resolving disputes, noting that the region had long relied on community-based mechanisms to uphold fairness and settle grievances. On improving access to justice, he identified technology and legal aid as two essential instruments for overcoming geographical barriers. "In a land of such vast distances, technology can do what no road ever could," he said. The CJI also underlined the importance of legal aid, calling it a constitutional promise that no citizen should be denied justice because of poverty or disability. He stressed the need for legal awareness camps, para-legal volunteers, affordable legal representation, lok adalats and timely compensation for victims of crime. "Access to justice, after all, begins not in the court's compound, but at the litigant's door," he said, expressing confidence that the Ladakh Legal Services Authority and the court's Legal Services Committee would work together to reach people awaiting justice in remote areas. The CJI spoke of a young child studying in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra who might one day argue a case before the court or even serve as a judge on its bench. "When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh, but taken root here," Justice Kant said.

body: Ladakh Lt Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena called the day a landmark milestone, fulfilling a long-standing demand for a court closer to home.
"A new era of accessible justice begins in Ladakh!

Deeply grateful to Chief Justice of India, for inaugurating the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of J&K and Ladakh, today at Leh, in the gracious presence of Supreme Court Judges and the Chief Justice and other companion Judges of the High Court of J&K and Ladakh," Saxena said on X after the event.

He said the Ladakh Bench of the High Court and the CJI's successive visits to the Union Territory within six months reflect his commitment to ensuring "access to justice" to all, particularly to remote communities in Ladakh.
"My sincere thanks and gratitude to the Prime Minister, Narendra Modi and Home Minister, Amit Shah, for consistently guiding Ladakh on the path of prosperity and inclusive development," he said.
Justice Surya Kant inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court at the High Court Complex, Melangthong, Leh.
The inauguration has been hailed as an important occasion in Ladakh's institutional development.

stories.headline: Menstrual hygiene: SC expresses displeasure over states, UTs not responding to Centre
stories.title: Menstrual hygiene: SC expresses displeasure over states, UTs not responding to Centre
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 18: The Supreme Court has expressed displeasure over states and Union territories not responding to the Centre on how its judgment declaring menstrual hygiene as a part of the fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution is being implemented. “If what we have said in the judgment is only going to remain on paper, how is the Union, states/UTs going to give effect to this fundamental right?” a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and R Mahadevan said. It said the apex court had declared menstrual hygiene/menstrual health as one of the facets of Article 21 of the Constitution, which deals with the protection of life and personal liberty. The bench said that on September 1, it had directed the states and UTs to take into consideration the deficiencies highlighted by it and report in that regard by the next date of hearing. In a significant judgment delivered on January 30, the apex court said that the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to menstrual health. During the hearing in the matter on October 13, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the bench that the Union of India has taken up this issue very seriously with all the states and UTs to respond in what manner the judgment is being implemented. “Unfortunately, the states/UTs have not responded to the Union so far. We fail to understand that once the Union calls for the necessary information, why the states/UTs do not respond,” the bench said. “We are sure that the Union, the states/UTs have realised the importance of the judgment that we delivered, declaring menstrual hygiene as a part of the fundamental right,” it said. The bench said the apex court's verdict was in the interest of young girls who were giving up education, more particularly, in remote parts of the country because of the problem of menstrual hygiene, etc. “We direct the Union to take up this issue very seriously with each state/UT and call for the necessary information in writing as to what steps they have taken so far for giving effect to the judgment delivered by this court,” it said. The bench said the Centre should study the verdict once again and accordingly call for information on each and every aspect of the matter. “On the next date of hearing, if we hear from the Union that some of the states/UTs have not responded, we shall proceed to issue contempt notice to the concerned chief secretary,” the bench said. While granting one last opportunity to do the needful, it posted the matter for next hearing on December 14. In its September 1 order, the bench had said the focus should be on the number of schools that lack gender-segregated, functional toilets with usable water connectivity, ensuring accessibility and privacy. The Centre had then informed the top court that 30,458 gender-segregated toilets with washing facilities have been constructed in schools across the country while 4,236 were under construction. In its judgment delivered in January, the apex court had directed the states and UTs to ensure that every school, whether government-run or privately managed, in both urban and rural areas, was provided with functional, gender-segregated toilets with usable water connectivity. The top court had also directed the states and UTs to ensure that every school provides sanitary napkins to girl students free of cost. The judgment was delivered on a plea seeking pan-India implementation of the Centre’s ‘menstrual hygiene policy for schoolgoing girls’ in government and government-aided schools from classes 6 to 12.

stories.headline: Supreme Court formed panel launches portal for complaints on violence at Jantar Mantar
stories.title: Supreme Court formed panel launches portal for complaints on violence at Jantar Mantar
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: NEW DELHI: The High Powered Enquiry Committee (HPEC), constituted by the Supreme Court of India to investigate all aspects of the incidents of violence at Jantar Mantar and other places outside Delhi in July 2026, has launched a portal to receive complaints, representations and information from affected persons and other stakeholders on Saturday.

The portal, http://hpec.nic.in, has been designed in such a manner as to enable due protection to vulnerable witnesses and also to keep the identities confidential and undisclosed, if so wished by the affected persons, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) informed through a statement.
As per the MHA, the affected persons and other stakeholders are encouraged to access the portal and upload their complaints and representations, making use of the formats as applicable.
"The portal is launched for the convenience of the affected people, including the affected police personnel," the MHA mentioned in the communique.

Apart from that, the ministry further said that any person wishing to provide information and suggestions relating to the issues referred to the HPEC under the Orders dated August 18, 2026 and September 10, 2026 may also do so through the portal.

Those who wish to submit the complaints, representations and other relevant material physically can do so at the Office of the HPEC at Shiksha Sadan, 17, Rouse Avenue Institutional Area, New Delhi 110002 between 2 pm and 4 pm on all working days.
Submissions can also be sent by post at the above address or by email at hpec2026.enquiry[at]nic[dot]in.
The Supreme Court had constituted the HPEC to enquire into all aspects of the incidents relating to violence at Jantar Mantar and at places outside Delhi during the month of July 2026.

stories.headline: IMD update: Heavy rain belt may shift to Kerala, parts of Karnataka this week
stories.title: IMD update: Heavy rain belt may shift to Kerala, parts of Karnataka this week
stories.summary: A vigorous north-east monsoon dumps extremely heavy rain (21 cm+) over Tamil Nadu and heavy rain (7-11 cm) over Coastal AP, Rayalaseema, Telangana, and South Interior Karnataka on Saturday
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The north-east monsoon is gathering strength over the South Peninsula, with isolated heavy rainfall likely over Kerala and Mahe and South Interior Karnataka for next six days until Saturday, and over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema for three days until Wednesday, India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said.

The 24 hours ending Sunday morning saw extremely heavy rainfall of 21 cm or more over Tamil Nadu, while Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Rayalaseema, Telangana and South Interior Karnataka received heavy rain of 7-11 cm.
The core of rainfall activity is now expected to shift towards Kerala and South Interior Karnataka this week.
Cyclonic circulations and a trough are working in tandem to sustain widespread moisture over the South Peninsula.
On Sunday afternoon, one circulation lay over west-central Bay of Bengal and adjoining coasts of south Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, while another persisted over North Interior Karnataka.
A trough extended from Lakshadweep to the west-central Bay across Karnataka and south Andhra Pradesh.
Meanwhile, a low-pressure area has developed over south-west Arabian Sea, more than 2,300 km off Kerala coast, and may intensify another round by Monday.
Its distance makes an immediate impact on southern India’s weather unlikely.
Global forecasts, however, point to the possibility of a successor system developing closer to home over Lakshadweep later this week, in response to an evolving system over the Bay of Bengal.
The IMD on Sunday flagged an upper-air cyclonic circulation over the Gulf of Thailand, backed by super typhoon Champi currently approaching the Philippines and watching from behind.
The incoming circulation is expected to move into Andaman Sea, descend to lower atmospheric levels and consolidate into a ‘low’ over the Bay.
The IMD’s numerical weather model indicate the circulation could intensify by a couple of notches October 28 (Saturday).

stories.headline: India's GDP per capita catching up with richer nations, growth worth celebrating: Korean economist
stories.title: India's GDP per capita catching up with richer nations, growth worth celebrating: Korean economist
stories.summary: The economist pointed to India's rising per capita income and a sharp decline in poverty to argue that the country's economic transformation over the past three decades, particularly the last 10 years, deserves greater attention
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Kim, Head of the India and South Asia Team at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (KIEP), said on Sunday that his earlier assessment of India's medium-term growth prospects had attracted comments suggesting that India remained poor.
"A more useful question is whether living standards are rising rapidly and whether India is CATCHING UP," he wrote in a detailed post on X.
According to the figures shared by Kim, India's GDP per capita stood at $2,702 in 2025, or $11,784 when adjusted for purchasing power parity (PPP).
